terms.comment: To judge good and approve; its other senses are “test” and “prove, show” (see prove).

evidence: Cic. Imp. Pomp. 69: laudō vehementissimēque comprobō (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Stronger and more formal: to approve wholeheartedly, or to ratify a decision.

phrases.latin: quicquid probat illa, probātō; quod dīcet, dīcās; quod negat illa, negēs
phrases.english: whatever she approves, approve; what she says, say; what she denies, deny

phrases.latin: istam tuam sententiam laudō vehementissimēque comprobō
phrases.english: I praise that view of yours and approve it most heartily

sources: Lewis & Short: probo · Lewis & Short: comprobo
